Theme

Body, health & movement

screw verb

have sex with (vulgar)

also have sex with, sleep with, bonk, shag, fuck, lay

classical

Ter. Hec. 3.3.33; Cic. Fat. 13.30 (Lewis & Short)

concumbō, concumbere, concubuī, concubitum

verb, third conjugation, with cum + ablative · Conjugation on Wiktionary

sleep with, have sex with

The plain word: literally “lie together”. With cum and the ablative of the partner: cum virō concumbere (Cic. Inv. 1.29.44, Lewis & Short). Latin has no neutral word that is also slang, so the coarse English verbs are given here by register below.

Other words

  • coeō, coīre, coiī, coitum — have sex, copulate (of people and animals)

    verb, irregular, with cum + ablative · also used · classical · Quint. 7.3.10: cum aliēnā uxōre (Lewis & Short); Lucr. 4.1055 (Lewis & Short) · Conjugation on Wiktionary

  • futuō, futuere, futuī, futūtum — fuck (of a man, with a woman as object)

    verb, third conjugation · also used · classical · Catull. 97.9; Mart. 10.81.1; 3.87.1 (Lewis & Short) · Conjugation on Wiktionary

    (vōx obscēna: Catull., Mart.)

    The obscene verb; Lewis & Short calls it rare, which means only that the authors who write it are few.

  • battuō, battuere, battuī — bang (literally, beat)

    verb, third conjugation · also used · classical · Cic. Fam. 9.22.4 (Lewis & Short: in mal. part.) · Conjugation on Wiktionary

    (vōx obscēna: Cic. Fam. 9.22.4)

    Properly to beat or pound; Cicero lists it among words with an obscene second sense. Traupman 375 gives the compound dēbattuere, which is not found in Lewis & Short.

  • dēbattuō, dēbattuere — screw (sexually)

    verb, third conjugation · also used · modern · Traupman 375 · Conjugation on Wiktionary

    (vōx obscēna)

    Traupman’s word, not found in Lewis & Short or the loci collections; Traupman is our only evidence.

  • subigitō, subigitāre — have sex with (illicitly); not “fondle”

    verb, first conjugation · also used · classical · Plaut. Mil. 3.1.53; Ter. Heaut. 3.3.6 (Lewis & Short); Traupman 359: fondle · Conjugation on Wiktionary

    (vōx cōmica: Plaut., Ter.)

    Lewis & Short: “to lie with illicitly (ante-class.)”. Traupman gives it for “fondle” and inter sē subigitāre for petting, which is milder than the word.

See also sex, fondle, play around with, prostitute.
